app.name: WiiKart
app.long_description: Semi-sim racing over nine circuits: seven stylized Colorado mountain passes with real grades, switchbacks, cliffs, and gravity, a flat speedway, and a wide, barriered oval with grandstands and real, gentle banking in its turns. Every circuit has its own weather (snow that melts into ice and then a puddle) behind a race-setup toggle. Braking now shares one grip budget with cornering, so braking in a straight line and getting back on the power as a corner opens out genuinely carries more speed than dragging the brake to the apex — real trail-braking technique, rewarded by the physics itself, for every AI driver as much as for you. Off the throttle, real engine braking holds the car back instead of coasting like a golf cart, a simple traction control trims power the instant the tires are already sliding, and brake lights actually light up. Every car is naturally aspirated (free to be built bigger, with no weight penalty for skipping forced induction), turbocharged (real lag), supercharged (instant, smaller bonus), or twin-turbocharged (the biggest bonus and the most weight of the four). Hard tires grip best in the dry and worst the moment the road is wet, icy, or snowed over; grip itself is no longer a free number — it follows from how light and how aerodynamically clean a car actually is. Eleven fallible AI rivals use different strategies and driver personalities, learn from mistakes, hunt the real racing line every track's own geometry hints at, and range from careful to three no-guts-no-glory drivers who commit to everything and pay for it in falls. Every car has its own drivetrain — front, rear, or all-wheel drive. Thirteen cars in the garage, edit any of them (built-ins included) or design your own from scratch. No collectible power-ups. Every on-screen speed, distance and weight reads in mph, feet and pounds. Cars, game settings, and keyboard/GameCube/Xbox control guidance are editable in documented JSON files. Includes lap timing and a live leaderboard, a marshal helicopter for driving the wrong way, an optional Dolphin input translator, per-track lap counts, garage, manual gearboxes with paddle-shifter defaults, tire strategy, staged cliff recovery, up to 4-player split screen, and procedural audio. Supports Wii Remote, Nunchuk, Classic Controller, GameCube pads, Xbox pads through Dolphin, and USB keyboard. Runs on Wii hardware and in Dolphin.
